correctness.rationale: The normalized Gaussian integral is reconstructed exactly. Local relative modes cancel, the collective replica matrix is \(M=2\alpha I+eK\), \(K\le2NI\), and the \(2N\) eigenspace is proved one-dimensional from common invariance under the replica cycles. With \(\lambda=(\alpha+Ne)/\alpha=(N-1)/(N^2a^2)+O(a^{-4})\), the determinant has one linear soft factor and all other factors stay positive, yielding the stated exponents, constant, and \(O(a^{-2})\) remainder. Finite checks reproduce independent closed forms from the source but are not used as the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating source explicitly leaves the all-\(n\), all-\(N\) coefficient as a conjecture. Searches of the exact title, formula, Gaussian replica terminology, and unitary-localization aliases found no covering proof. The closest older theorem localizes block correlations but studies another entanglement quantity and does not imply the replica singularity.
residual_risks: An equivalent replica-nullity argument could exist in older literature under remote multi-invariant or Gaussian-integral terminology not surfaced by the searches.
The result is only for integer replica order; it does not settle analytic continuation to noninteger \(n\) or \(n=1\).

value.rationale: The result proves an explicit 2026 conjecture for all previously open integer replica orders and all finite mode partitions, provides the first uniform \(O(a^{-2})\) remainder in that setting, and gives a concrete determinant expression for the partition-dependent constant. This is a structural theorem rather than a recomputation of a tabulated case.
